title: Computational complexity conjecture for the alpha-permanent
statement:
Let $M$ be a matrix and let $\operatorname{per}_{\alpha}M$ denote its alpha-permanent. For a positive integer $k$, the notation $\#P$ refers to the relevant counting-complexity class, and $P$ to deterministic polynomial time.

**Computational complexity conjecture.** Computation of the $\alpha$-permanent is $\#P$-complete, except for

$$
\alpha\in\{-1,\ldots,-K\},
$$

for some $K\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$. The complexity for $\alpha\in\{-2,-3,\ldots\}$ lies somewhere between $P$ and $\#P$ and is monotonically non-decreasing as $\alpha$ decreases.

The paper notes that the computational complexity of the alpha-permanent had not been studied and leaves open the possibility that $K=1$, in which case only $\alpha=-1$ is exceptional. The authors further identify the central expectation as $\#P$-completeness unless $\alpha$ is a negative integer.
source_name: Harry Crane, “Some algebraic identities for the alpha-permanent”, arXiv:1304.1772 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.1772

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).
